# Ezekiel 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD's message came to me:

**2** "What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: 'The parents eat sour grapes, but it's the children who get the sour taste'?

**3** As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.

**4** Every living soul belongs to Me — parent and child alike. And this is My rule: The person who sins is the one who dies.

**5** Suppose a man is truly good and does what is right and just.

**6** He doesn't worship idols on the hilltops or look to the false gods of Israel. He doesn't sleep with another man's wife or with a woman during her period.

**7** He doesn't exploit anyone. He returns what a borrower puts up as collateral. He doesn't rob. He gives food to the hungry and clothes to those who need them.

**8** He doesn't charge interest on loans or make a profit by cheating. He refuses to do wrong and judges fairly between people.

**9** He follows My laws and faithfully obeys My commands. That man is righteous, and he will surely live, declares the Lord GOD.

**10** But suppose that good man has a violent son — a murderer who commits terrible sins.

**11** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**12** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**13** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**14** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**15** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**16** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**17** Even though the father did everything right, this son will die for his own sins. He is responsible for his own blood.

**18** But the father — if he was an extortioner who robbed people and did what was wrong — he will die for his own sins.

**19** "'But that's not fair!' you protest. 'Why shouldn't the son pay for his father's sins?' Because the son did what was right and carefully followed all My commands — he will live.

**20** The person who sins is the one who will die. Children will not be punished for their parents' sins, and parents will not be punished for their children's sins. Righteous people will be rewarded for their own righteousness, and wicked people will suffer for their own wickedness.

**21** But if wicked people turn away from all their sins and begin to obey My laws and do what is right and just — they will surely live and not die.

**22** All their past sins will be forgotten. Because of the righteous things they are now doing, they will live.

**23** Do you think I enjoy seeing wicked people die?" asks the Lord GOD. "Of course not! I want them to turn from their wicked ways and live!

**24** But if righteous people turn from their righteous behavior and start doing all the same disgusting things wicked people do — should they be allowed to live? No! All their previous goodness will be forgotten. They will die for their sins.

**25** Yet you say, 'The Lord isn't being fair!' Listen, people of Israel — am I the one who's not fair, or is it you?

**26** So I will judge each of you according to your own actions, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD. Turn from your sins! Don't let them destroy you!

**27** So I will judge each of you according to your own actions, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD. Turn from your sins! Don't let them destroy you!

**28** So I will judge each of you according to your own actions, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD. Turn from your sins! Don't let them destroy you!

**29** So I will judge each of you according to your own actions, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD. Turn from your sins! Don't let them destroy you!

**30** I will judge each of you according to your actions, declares the Lord GOD. Repent! Turn from all your sins, so that they won't be your downfall.

**31** Throw off all the sins you've committed. Get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why should you die, people of Israel?

**32** I don't want anyone to die, declares the Lord GOD. So turn back and live!"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **18:2-4**: People love blaming their parents — 'We're suffering because of what they did.' God says: Stop. Every person stands or falls on their own choices. That's liberating and terrifying at the same time.

- **18:23**: This might be the most important verse in Ezekiel: 'Do I enjoy watching the wicked die? Of course not!' God is not a punisher who delights in suffering. He's a father who desperately wants His children to come home.

- **18:31-32**: The passionate plea at the end is almost startling after so many chapters of judgment: 'Why would you choose death? Turn around and LIVE!' God sounds almost desperate. That desperation is love.

— PNEUMA
